subproblem.title: Simon Ch. 2, 4.3: the classical (curve) tangent space at a C² Simon chart point equals the range of the chart derivative
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, M, W ⊆ ℝ^N, D ⊆ ℝ^n, and let φ : ℝ^n → ℝ^N be a C² local representation of M in Simon's sense (Ch. 2, 4.1; Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 2 M D W φ). This means D and W are open, φ is C² on D and injective on D, φ(D) = W ∩ M, φ is relatively proper (K ⊆ W compact ⇒ D ∩ φ⁻¹(K) compact), and Dφ(u) is injective for every u ∈ D. Let a ∈ D. Then classicalTangentSpace M (φ(a)) equals the range of Dφ(a) = fderiv ℝ φ a. Here classicalTangentSpace M (φ(a)) is the set of velocities γ'(0) of maps γ : ℝ → ℝ^N that are C¹ on (−1,1), map (−1,1) into M, and satisfy γ(0) = φ(a).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (M W : Set (Euclidean N)) (D : Set (Euclidean n)) (φ : Euclidean n → Euclidean N) (a : Euclidean n), Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 2 M D W φ → a ∈ D → classicalTangentSpace M (φ a) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ φ a)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory, Ch. 2 §4. There T_yM is defined as the set of velocities of C¹ curves (−1,1) → M through y, and 4.3 (printed p. 55) says: "One readily checks that T_yM is a linear subspace of ℝ^{n+ℓ} with basis D_1φ(x), …, D_nφ(x), where φ is any local representation as in 4.1 above with φ(x) = y." The book leaves this check to the reader. What follows is step 1 of the parent proof of root.constancy-a1 written out in full, for C² representations (the case used by ConstancyTheorem).

Hypotheses and notation. N, n ∈ ℕ; M, W ⊆ ℝ^N; D ⊆ ℝ^n; φ : ℝ^n → ℝ^N with Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation 2 M D W φ, i.e.:
(i) D and W are open;
(ii) φ is C² on D;
(iii) φ is injective on D;
(iv) φ(D) = W ∩ M;
(v) relative properness: K ⊆ W compact ⇒ D ∩ φ⁻¹(K) compact;
(vi) Dφ(u) is injective for every u ∈ D.
Fix a ∈ D and write L := Dφ(a) = fderiv ℝ φ a. By definition, ξ ∈ classicalTangentSpace M y iff there is γ : ℝ → ℝ^N, C¹ on (−1,1), with γ((−1,1)) ⊆ M, γ(0) = y and HasDerivAt γ ξ 0. Claim: classicalTangentSpace M (φ(a)) = range L = Set.range (fderiv ℝ φ a).

1. φ is differentiable at a with derivative L. D is an open neighbourhood of a and φ is C² on D, so φ is C² at a (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). In particular φ is Fréchet differentiable at a, with derivative fderiv ℝ φ a = L.

2. range L ⊆ classicalTangentSpace M (φ(a)). Let ξ = L w with w ∈ ℝ^n.
 2a. Since D is open, choose r > 0 with the open ball B(a, r) ⊆ D. Set ε := r/(‖w‖+1) > 0, c(t) := a + (ε sin(t/ε)) w for t ∈ ℝ, and γ := φ ∘ c.
 2b. c(t) ∈ D for every t ∈ ℝ, because ‖c(t) − a‖ = |ε sin(t/ε)|·‖w‖ ≤ ε‖w‖ = r‖w‖/(‖w‖+1) < r.
 2c. γ is C¹ on (−1,1). The map c is C^∞ on ℝ: a constant plus the smooth scalar function t ↦ ε sin(t/ε) times the fixed vector w. Its values lie in D by 2b, and φ is C², hence C¹, on D. A map that is C¹ on D composed with a C¹ map into D is C¹ on all of ℝ.
 2d. γ maps (−1,1) into M: γ(t) = φ(c(t)) ∈ φ(D) = W ∩ M ⊆ M by (iv).
 2e. γ(0) = φ(a + (ε sin 0) w) = φ(a).
 2f. HasDerivAt γ ξ 0. The scalar map t ↦ ε sin(t/ε) has derivative ε·cos(0/ε)·(1/ε) = 1 at 0, so c has derivative w at 0. Since c(0) = a and φ has derivative L at a (step 1), the chain rule gives γ'(0) = L w = ξ.
 Hence ξ ∈ classicalTangentSpace M (φ(a)).

3. A local defining map at φ(a), from the inverse function theorem and relative properness. There are an open A ⊆ ℝ^N with φ(a) ∈ A and a map F : ℝ^N → ℝ^N such that F is C² on A, F = 0 on M ∩ A, and ker DF(φ(a)) = range L. Construction:
 3a. L is injective by (vi), so there is a linear P : ℝ^N → ℝ^n with P ∘ L = id.
 3b. g := P ∘ φ is C² near a, and Dg(a) = P ∘ L = id is invertible. By the C² inverse function theorem there is a C² local inverse η of g at g(a), with η(g(u)) = u for all u in a neighbourhood of a.
 3c. ψ := η ∘ P is C² near φ(a), ψ(φ(a)) = a, and ψ(φ(u)) = u for all u near a. Differentiating ψ ∘ φ = id at a gives Dψ(φ(a)) ∘ L = id.
 3d. Pick an open D₀ with a ∈ D₀ ⊆ D on which ψ ∘ φ = id. By (ii)–(v), φ is a continuous, injective, proper map of D onto W ∩ M, hence a homeomorphism onto W ∩ M (Simon Ch. 2, 4.2). So there is an open A₀ ⊆ W with φ(D₀) = A₀ ∩ M, and φ(a) ∈ A₀.
 3e. Define F(y) := y − φ(ψ(y)). F is C² on an open B ∋ φ(a), since ψ is C² near φ(a) and φ is C² near ψ(φ(a)) = a. Put A := A₀ ∩ B. If y ∈ M ∩ A, then y ∈ A₀ ∩ M = φ(D₀), so y = φ(u) with u ∈ D₀ and F(y) = φ(u) − φ(ψ(φ(u))) = 0.
 3f. By the chain rule, DF(φ(a)) = id − L ∘ Dψ(φ(a)). If DF(φ(a))v = 0, then v = L(Dψ(φ(a))v) ∈ range L. If v = L u, then L(Dψ(φ(a))(L u)) = L u by 3c, so DF(φ(a))v = 0. Hence ker DF(φ(a)) = range L.
 (This is exactly the kernel-checked SimonGMT lemma Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.exists_local_normal_defining_map, Chapter08/ConstancyNormalCharts.lean:90, applied to the given representation and a ∈ D. Its axioms are propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.)

4. classicalTangentSpace M (φ(a)) ⊆ range L. Let ξ belong to the left side, witnessed by γ (C¹ on (−1,1), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ M, γ(0) = φ(a), HasDerivAt γ ξ 0). Take A and F from step 3.
 4a. γ is differentiable, hence continuous, at 0, and γ(0) = φ(a) ∈ A with A open, so γ(t) ∈ A for all t near 0. Also (−1,1) is a neighbourhood of 0, so γ(t) ∈ M for all t near 0. Hence F(γ(t)) = 0 for all t near 0. So F ∘ γ agrees with the constant 0 on a neighbourhood of 0, and HasDerivAt (F ∘ γ) 0 0.
 4b. F is C² on the open set A ∋ γ(0), so F is differentiable at γ(0) = φ(a) with derivative DF(φ(a)). By the chain rule, HasDerivAt (F ∘ γ) (DF(φ(a))ξ) 0.
 4c. By uniqueness of derivatives, DF(φ(a))ξ = 0. So ξ ∈ ker DF(φ(a)) = range L (step 3f), i.e. ξ = L w for some w ∈ ℝ^n.
 (In the language of the parent proof: for t near 0, γ(t) ∈ A₀ ∩ M = φ(D₀), so γ = φ ∘ β near 0 with β := ψ ∘ γ differentiable at 0 and β(0) = a. Hence γ'(0) = L β'(0) ∈ range L. The vanishing of F ∘ γ near 0 is the same statement.)

5. Steps 2 and 4 give classicalTangentSpace M (φ(a)) = range L = Set.range (fderiv ℝ φ a). ∎

6. Formal route. This exact statement was proved in a scratch copy importing GMT.Ch08.Submission and Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.ConstancyNormalCharts, with axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.
 Setup: intro N n M W D φ a hφ ha; hφa := (hφ.contDiffOn a ha).contDiffAt (hφ.isOpen_source.mem_nhds ha); ext ξ; constructor.
 (⊆) rintro ⟨γ, -, hmaps, hγ0, hder⟩. Then obtain ⟨A, F, hAo, haA, hF, hFM, hker⟩ := exists_local_normal_defining_map hφ ha. Get HasFDerivAt for F at γ 0 from ((hF (φ a) haA).contDiffAt (hAo.mem_nhds haA)).differentiableAt after rw [hγ0], and use HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt 0 hder. Show eventual vanishing with filter_upwards [hder.continuousAt.preimage_mem_nhds (by rw [hγ0]; exact hAo.mem_nhds haA), Ioo_mem_nhds _ _] and hFM ⟨hmaps ht2, ht1⟩. Use (hasDerivAt_const 0 0).congr_of_eventuallyEq and HasDerivAt.unique to get fderiv ℝ F (φ a) ξ = 0, i.e. ξ ∈ (fderiv ℝ F (φ a)).ker. Rewrite with hker and destructure ⟨w, hw⟩.
 (⊇) rintro ⟨w, rfl⟩. Use Metric.isOpen_iff.mp hφ.isOpen_source a ha and c t := a + (ε * Real.sin (t / ε)) • w. Get ContDiff ℝ 1 c from contDiff_const.add (ContDiff.smul (contDiff_const.mul (Real.contDiff_sin.comp (contDiff_id.div_const ε))) contDiff_const), then (hφ.contDiffOn.of_le _).comp_contDiff hc hcD. Use hφ.image_eq for MapsTo. For the derivative use Real.hasDerivAt_sin, HasDerivAt.comp, div_const, const_mul, smul_const, const_add, and finally HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt.
proof_key_steps: Since D is open and φ is C² on D, φ is differentiable at a with derivative L = Dφ(a).
range L ⊆ classical tangent space: for ξ = Lw take γ(t) = φ(a + ε sin(t/ε) w) with ε = r/(‖w‖+1) and B(a,r) ⊆ D. Then γ is C¹, lies in φ(D) ⊆ M, γ(0) = φ(a) and γ'(0) = Lw.

Local defining map (inverse function theorem on P∘φ plus relative properness; SimonGMT exists_local_normal_defining_map): an open A ∋ φ(a) and F, C² on A, with F = 0 on M ∩ A and ker DF(φ(a)) = range L.
Classical tangent space ⊆ range L: F∘γ ≡ 0 near 0, so DF(φ(a))γ'(0) = 0 by the chain rule and uniqueness of derivatives.
The two inclusions give classicalTangentSpace M (φ a) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ φ a).

audit.reason: The prose includes every local-representation hypothesis and exactly matches the independently elaborated proposition. The bounded sine curve realizes every derivative-range vector while remaining in D. Conversely, relative properness and the inverse-function construction supply a defining map whose derivative kernel is the chart range; differentiating its locally vanishing composition with the witnessing curve proves the reverse inclusion. The supplied proof is complete, non-circular, and directly formalizable. The declaration name is a fresh bare identifier.

subproblem.title: Constancy Theorem 8.4.1 in measure form (corrected): V is c·H^n⌞(M ∩ U) pushed onto the classical tangent graph
subproblem.statement: Let V be an n-varifold in the open set U ⊆ ℝ^N (Varifold N n U) that is stationary in U. Let M ⊆ ℝ^N be an n-dimensional C² submanifold in Simon's sense (IsSimonSubmanifold 2 M). Assume U ∩ spt μ_V ⊆ M, M ∩ U is preconnected, and M is nonempty. Then there are c ∈ [0,∞] with c ≠ ∞ and a Borel measurable map T : ℝ^N → G(N,n) such that V equals (c · H^n ⌞ (M ∩ U)) pushed forward under x ↦ (x, T(x)), as measures on ℝ^N × G(N,n) with H^n = μHE[n]. Moreover, if c ≠ 0, then for every x ∈ M ∩ U the plane of T(x) equals classicalTangentSpace M x, as subsets of ℝ^N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (M : Set (Euclidean N)), V.Stationary → Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Euclidean n) 2 M → U ∩ V.weight.support ⊆ M → IsPreconnected (M ∩ U) → M.Nonempty → ∃ (c : ℝ≥0∞) (T : Euclidean N → Grassmannian N n), c ≠ ∞ ∧ Measurable T ∧ V.measure = (c • (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)).restrict (M ∩ U)).map (fun x ↦ (x, T x)) ∧ (c ≠ 0 → ∀ x ∈ M ∩ U, ((T x).plane : Set (Euclidean N)) = classicalTangentSpace M x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 4.1 and its printed proof (pp. 213–214): displays (1)–(5) and the final paragraph.
Erratum (GMT/Ch08/README.md; SimonGMT ConstancyDomainCounterexample.counterexample_constancy_printed_hypotheses): the printed hypothesis "M connected" is replaced by "M ∩ U (pre)connected", and V = θ₀ v(M) is read in U. Counterexample to the printed version: U = ℝ∖{0}, M = ℝ, V = v((0,∞)) is stationary in U with spt ⊆ M, but it is not a constant multiple of v(M ∩ U). Connectedness of M ∩ U is exactly what the last line of the printed proof uses.
This child is the measure form "V = θ₀ v(M ∩ U)" of the theorem, i.e. steps 2–5 and 7 of the parent proof of root.constancy-a1. The sibling classical_tangent (Simon Ch. 2, 4.3) converts chart tangent planes into classicalTangentSpace.
Notation: μ := μ_V = V.weight; G := G(N,n) = Grassmannian N n; H^n := μHE[n]; p_S is orthogonal projection onto S; spt is support.

Hypotheses. V ∈ Varifold N n U with U open, and V is stationary in U (δV(X) = 0 for all X ∈ K(U;ℝ^N)). M is an n-dimensional C² submanifold in Simon's sense (IsSimonSubmanifold 2 M). U ∩ spt μ ⊆ M. M ∩ U is preconnected. M ≠ ∅.
Claim. There are c ∈ [0,∞] with c ≠ ∞ and a Borel T : ℝ^N → G such that V = (c · H^n⌞(M ∩ U)).map(x ↦ (x, T(x))). Moreover, if c ≠ 0, then ((T(x)).plane : Set ℝ^N) = classicalTangentSpace M x for every x ∈ M ∩ U.

1. Printed (1)–(2). Let f ∈ C²_c(U) vanish on M ∩ U. Then X := f∇f ∈ K(U;ℝ^N), and by 2.3
 div_S(f∇f) = ∇^S f·∇f + f div_S ∇f = |p_S(∇f)|² + f div_S ∇f.
 V is carried by G_n(U ∩ spt μ), and U ∩ spt μ ⊆ M ∩ U, where f = 0. Hence δV(f∇f) = ∫|p_S(∇f(x))|² dV(x,S) (printed (1)). Since δV = 0 and (x,S) ↦ |p_S(∇f(x))|² is continuous and ≥ 0, p_S(∇f(x)) = 0 for every (x,S) ∈ spt V with x ∈ U (printed (2)).
 [SimonGMT Varifold.Stationary.project_gradient_eq_zero_of_vanishing, ConstancySupport.lean:139.]

2. Printed (3). Let (x,S) ∈ spt V with x ∈ U.
 2a. x ∈ U ∩ spt μ ⊆ M, so by IsSimonSubmanifold x ∈ W ∩ M = φ(D) for a Simon C² representation φ : D → W ∩ M; write x = φ(a) with a ∈ D.
 2b. By the inverse function theorem and relative properness (Simon Ch. 2, 4.2) there are an open A ∋ x and F : ℝ^N → ℝ^N, C² on A, with F = 0 on M ∩ A and ker DF(x) = range Dφ(a). Here F = id − φ∘ψ, with ψ a C² local left inverse of φ [SimonGMT exists_local_normal_defining_map, ConstancyNormalCharts.lean:90].
 2c. Take a cutoff ζ ∈ C^∞_c(A ∩ U) with ζ = 1 near x, and let f_j := ζ·F_j for j = 1,…,N. Then f_j ∈ C²_c(U), and f_j = 0 on M ∩ U: on M ∩ A because F = 0 there, elsewhere because ζ = 0. Also ∇f_j(x) = ∇F_j(x) because F(x) = 0. So the ∇f_j(x) span the row space (ker DF(x))^⊥ = (range Dφ(a))^⊥.
 2d. Step 1 gives p_S(v) = 0 for all v ∈ (range Dφ(a))^⊥, i.e. (range Dφ(a))^⊥ ⊆ S^⊥, so S ⊆ range Dφ(a). Both are n-dimensional (Dφ(a) is injective), hence S = range Dφ(a) (printed (3)).
 [SimonGMT Stationary.plane_le_ker_fderiv_of_local_level_set; Stationary.plane_eq_parametrizedTangent, ConstancyNormalCharts.lean:188.]
 2e. In particular, for x ∈ U the fibre {S : (x,S) ∈ spt V} has at most one element, and range Dφ(a) does not depend on the chart (parametrizedTangent_eq_of_overlap).

3. Printed (4).
 3a. G is compact, so spt μ = π(spt V), where π(x,S) = x. Hence for x ∈ U ∩ spt μ the fibre is exactly one plane T(x), and x ↦ T(x) is continuous on U ∩ spt μ (closed graph into the compact G).
 3b. Since M ≠ ∅, a chart gives an n-plane P₀ = range Dφ(a₀) ∈ G. Setting T := P₀ off U ∩ spt μ gives a Borel map T : ℝ^N → G (U ∩ spt μ is Borel).
 3c. V is concentrated on spt V ∩ (U × G), which lies in the graph {(x, T(x)) : x ∈ U ∩ spt μ}. Hence V = μ.map(x ↦ (x, T(x))), i.e. ∫ f(x,S) dV(x,S) = ∫ f(x, T(x)) dμ(x) (printed (4)).
 [SimonGMT Stationary.exists_measurable_tangentGraph, ConstancyTangentGraph.lean:120.]

4. Printed (5).
 4a. V is stationary in every open ball contained in U, so by monotonicity (Ch. 8, 3.3/3.4) θ(x) := Θ^n(μ, x) exists and is finite at every x ∈ U.
